note: 02A: pins the regression that must fail if a later cleanup aliases `set` to `setq` or resolves its target through the lexical environment instead of the global value cell. `set` always writes the symbol's global value cell; a lexical binding of the same spelling is neither read nor changed. Inside the inner lambda, the lexical `x` is 1, `(set 'x 2)` returns 2 and leaves the lexical `x` at 1 (so the inner list is `(2 1)`), and the global `x` -- set to 9 by the outer `(setq x 9)`, which has no enclosing lexical binding -- becomes 2. Checked under lexical evaluation (the oracle shim's `(eval form t)`). Fe has no `set` binding yet -- standalone Fe reports void-function.
